title: 文王既沒文不在茲乎
summary: Confucius's declaration that the cultural tradition resides in him after King Wen's passing, exemplifying his sense of mission to transmit the Way.

sources.question: 文王既沒，文不在茲乎？ 何意味？
sources.title: 文王既沒，文不在茲乎？ 何意味？

slug: 一獻質三獻文五獻察七獻神
title: 一獻質三獻文五獻察七獻神 / Seven Offerings: The Hierarchy of Ritual Refinement
summary: The graduated progression of seven ritual offerings from simple (質) to spiritual (神).

title: 一言僨事一人定國
summary: 一人言行，足以傾覆邦國或安定天下。

title: 一身之迷不足傾
summary: 一人之迷不足害，若天下皆迷，則無由以正之。

title: 七十里為政於天下
summary: Mencius cited Tang's rule over all under heaven with only seventy li, showing that benevolent government, not territory, determines legitimate sovereignty.

title: Seven Halls System / 七廟
summary: The hierarchical ancestral temple system for kings, featuring five immediate ancestor halls and two distant ancestor shrines, with regulations for offering frequency and the progression from hall to altar to spirit.

title: 國有七患
summary: 治國當察七患，防患於未然。

title: 夏道尊命殷人尊神周人尊禮 / Governance of the Three Dynasties: Xia Honored Mandates, Shang Honored Spirits, Zhou Honored Ritual
summary: 比較夏、商、周三代政治文化之特徵，揭示三代治道之差異及其民風影響。

title: 三刺 / Triple Investigation in Judicial Process
summary: The threefold inquiry procedure in ancient Chinese judicial administration.

title: 三年之喪
summary: 稱情而立文，為至痛極也，孝子送死之定制。

title: 三年之隆
summary: 三年以為隆，緦小功以為殺，期九月以為間，隆殺有差。

title: 三日不生亦不生矣 / Three Days Without Revival Means No Revival
summary: 喪禮三日而斂，以俟其生；三日而不生則孝子之心亦衰，此聖人制禮之本意。

title: 三日成服
summary: 奔喪之禮，三日而成服，五哭而事畢。

title: 三無
summary: 無聲之樂、無體之禮、無服之喪，至道之所在。

title: 上不臣天子下不事諸侯
summary: 儒者有超然於世功名利祿之外者，雖分國如錙銖，不臣不仕。

title: 上易事下易知 / Easy Governance Through Uprightness
summary: The principle that when rulers are straightforward, governance becomes easy and people become intelligent.

title: Superior Righteousness / 上義
summary: 文子論上義之道，治國家、理境內、行仁義、布德施惠，霸王之治的最高境界。

title: 下齊如權衡 / The Hem Balanced Like a Scale
summary: 深衣裾下平齊如秤錘天秤，以象公平之心、持平之政。

title: 不以辭盡人 / Not Judging by Words Alone / 辭を以て人を尽くすこと勿れ
summary: The Confucian principle that a truly exemplary person should not be judged solely by their words, as words may be embellished while actions reveal true character.

title: 不動心
summary: 孟子四十不動心，告子先之。其要在持其志而勿暴其氣。

title: 不召之臣
summary: 大有為之君，當親就賢臣，不可輕召。

slug: 不奪人之喪亦不可奪喪
title: Not Depriving Others of Mourning, Nor Being Deprived / 不奪人之喪亦不可奪喪
summary: The ritual principle that mourning obligations must not be imposed upon others nor be arbitrarily taken away.

title: 不忍人之心
summary: 人皆有怵惕惻隱之心，先王本此心以行不忍人之政，故治天下可運之掌上。

title: 不怨天，不尤人
summary: 君子之於得失，歸諸天命，不歸咎於人。

title: 不言之教 / 不言之教 / Teaching Through Non-Speech
summary: Wenzi's doctrine that true governance and teaching operate through silent, effortless influence rather than verbal instruction.

title: 不隕獲於貧賤不充詘於富貴
summary: 儒者於貧賤不失其守，於富貴不增其傲，終始一節。

title: Refusing Contemptuous Charity / 不食嗟來之食
summary: The story of a starving man who would rather die than accept food offered with disdain, and the Confucian discussion of when dignity requires acceptance or rejection.

title: 世子之記 / The Heir Prince's Daily Code
summary: A detailed record of the heir prince's daily conduct, including morning inquiries, meals, and care during illness.

title: 世子齒學 / Heir Apparent Studying by Age
summary: 世子與國人齒讓，以明父子、長幼之道。

title: 中山公子牟
summary: 魏國賢公子，好與賢人游，悅公孫龍之學

title: 中庸
summary: 述天命、性、道、教之旨，明中和、誠明之義，兼論君子修身及聖人之道。

title: 乘勢待時
summary: 雖有智慧，不如乘勢；雖有鎡基，不如待時。時機既至而行王政，功半古之人必倍之。

title: Jiǔ Fāng Gāo Examines a Horse / 九方皋相馬
summary: The story of the horse expert who grasps the essential while ignoring the superficial.

title: 九經
summary: 治天下國家之九常法：脩身、尊賢、親親、敬大臣、體群臣、子庶民、來百工、柔遠人、懷諸侯。

title: 事人與事鬼
summary: 未能事人，焉能事鬼；未知生，焉知死。

title: 事君欲諫不欲陳 / Serving the Ruler: Advise, Do Not Boast
summary: Confucian teaching on the proper manner of serving rulers: one should offer sincere remonstrance but never publicize one's loyalty or good service.

title: Rulers Should Measure Before Entering / 事君者量而後入
summary: The Confucian principle that those serving rulers must first measure circumstances before entering into affairs.

title: 五等之人 / The Five Ranks of People
summary: A hierarchical taxonomy of twenty-five human types classified into five ranks, from divine transcendence to servile dependence.

title: 五兵 / The Five Types of Military Action
summary: A Daoist classification of military campaigns into five ethical categories: righteous, responsive, wrathful, greedy, and arrogant.

title: Fifty Steps Mocking One Hundred / 五十步笑百步
summary: 孟子以五十步笑百步之喻，批評梁惠王移民移粟之政與鄰國無異，皆非王道。

title: 五百年必有王者興
summary: 天命五百年間必有聖王及名世者出，己身適逢其時，當仁不讓。

title: The Five Sacrifices / 五祀
summary: The five categories of domestic and neighborhood sacrifices performed by rulers and officials according to rank.

title: 五穀為民食所仰
summary: 食為民天，農為國本。

title: 五至
summary: 志、詩、禮、樂、哀，五者相至相通，塞乎天地。

title: 五起
summary: 三無之義有五層漸進，自氣志不違而至施及孫子。

title: 五霸罪人
summary: 五霸非王道，乃諸侯之罪人；今之大夫，又諸侯之罪人。 pentarchy as criminals of the Three Kings.

slug: 人之所以異於禽獸者幾希
title: 人之所以異於禽獸者幾希
summary: 人禽之別，在於仁義，其分也微。

title: 人情 / Human Emotions and Desires
summary: The seven human emotions and desires that form the basis of social order and ritual according to the Yunyun chapter.

title: The Hundred-Year Life Stages / 人生百年
summary: The Confucian framework of life stages from age ten to one hundred, each with its proper name and appropriate conduct.

title: 人皆可以為堯舜
summary: 堯舜之道，非有他也，孝弟而已。

title: 人道之至文
summary: 三年之喪，禮之至文，乃百王古今之所同。

title: 什長亭尉
summary: 城上十人一什長，屬一吏士、一亭尉，以嚴守備之制。

title: 仁之難成 / The Difficulty of Perfecting Benevolence
summary: Confucius's lament that true benevolence is rare and difficult to achieve, yet remains the highest human virtue worth pursuing throughout one's life.

title: 仁者如射
summary: 仁者如射，射者正己而後發，發而不中，不怨勝己者，反求諸己而已矣。

title: 今之良臣古之民賊
summary: 能闢土地充府庫之臣，實古之所謂民賊也。

title: 仍舊貫
summary: 閔子騫以為仍用舊制，何必改作；夫子稱其言必中。

title: 以善養人
summary: 以善服人者未能服人，以善養人者然後能服天下。

title: 以德報怨 / Repaying Wrongdoing with Virtue
summary: A Confucian ethical principle advocating the response of virtue to resentment, balancing retributive justice with benevolent forgiveness.

title: 以德行仁者王
summary: 以力假仁者霸，必有大國；以德行仁者王，不待大。霸道非心服，力不贍故；王道心悅誠服，如七十子之服孔子。

title: 以意逆志 / Interpretation Through Intention / 意を以って志を逆らう
summary: A hermeneutical principle that one should grasp the author's true intention by intuiting meaning rather than being bound by literal wording.

title: 以政治國以奇用兵 / Govern the State with Rectitude, Fight with Surprise
summary: The fundamental Daoist military-political principle of governing through proper order and waging war through strategic deception.

title: 以燕伐燕
summary: 誅暴伐無道，必待天吏；若以燕伐燕，是同類相殘，不足為義師。

title: 伯夷隘
summary: 伯夷非其君不事，然其心狹隘；柳下惠不羞污君，然其行不恭。隘與不恭，君子不由。

title: 何必曰利 / On Not Speaking of Profit
summary: 孟子以利與仁義對舉，謂上下交征利則國危，惟行仁義可以王天下。

title: Wearing Jade / 佩玉
summary: The Confucian practice of wearing jade as a symbol of virtue and moral cultivation, with specific regulations governing its use by rank.

title: 侍坐言志
summary: 孔門四子侍坐，各言其志，夫子深許曾皙之沂浴。

title: 修身
summary: 存養心性以正身形，乃齊家治國之本

title: 偃師造人 / 偃師、偶人を作る
summary: The story of craftsman Yan Shi who created an artificial puppet so lifelike that King Mu mistook it for a real person, exploring the boundary between art and life.

title: 備城門
summary: 《墨子》篇名，述守城之法，兼及攻城十二術及城守之十四者。

title: 備梯
summary: 禦雲梯攻城之法。

title: 備者國之重也
summary: 備乃治國之要，無備則亡。

title: 先勞而後祿
summary: 儒者先盡其道而後受其祿，不以祿為先圖。

title: 先進後進
summary: 夫子自謂從先進之禮樂，不從後進之溫文。

title: 免麻
summary: 齊衰以下之喪，入門哭，免而袒麻，與主人共禮。

title: 內外之分 / The Division of Inner and Outer / 内外の分かれ
summary: The Confucian principle of gender-specific spatial division between males (outer/public) and females (inner/private) in household management.

title: 內形於外
summary: 有諸內者，必形諸外；賢否之效，自然而著。

title: 兩小兒辯日 / 二子の日の辯論
summary: A famous anecdote about two children debating whether the sun is closer in the morning or at noon, illustrating the limits of human knowledge.

title: 八州八伯 / Eight Provinces and Eight Regional Lords / 八州八伯
summary: 八州八伯 describes the territorial division of the Zhou realm into eight provinces each governed by a regional lord.

title: 公族之刑 / Criminal Justice for the Ducal Clan
summary: 公族犯死罪，雖親不以犯有司，正術也。

title: Exemption at the Duke's Gate / 公門有稅齊衰
summary: The principle that one need not remove mourning garments at the duke's gate, unlike at other official settings.

title: The Six Failings / 六失
summary: The potential moral distortions that arise when each of the Six Classics is improperly understood or applied.

title: The Six Teachings / 六教
summary: The Confucian doctrine that each of the Six Classics cultivates a specific moral disposition in those who study it.

title: 六經之教 / The Six Classics and Their Educational Functions
summary: Confucius's teaching that each of the six classics cultivates specific virtues while carrying inherent risks of excess.

title: 共牢而食 / Eating from the Same Offering / 同じ牢で食す
summary: 昏禮中夫婦同食一牲之禮，表夫婦同尊卑之恩義。

slug: 其往送也如慕其反也如疑
title: 其往送也如慕，其反也如疑 / Like Longing in Going, Like Hesitation in Returning
summary: 送喪之人，往時如子女之慕親，反時如有求而不得，狀孝子之心於送死之際。

title: Mourning Periods and Their Classifications / 再期之喪，三年也
summary: The systematic classification of mourning periods according to the Three Seasons framework, ranging from one season to three years.

title: 凱弟君子
summary: 詩所述和樂近善之君子，堪為民之父母。

title: Establishment of Collateral Lines / 別子為祖，繼別為宗
summary: The foundational principle of Chinese lineage systems where non-heir sons establish new ancestral lines, creating the major and minor lineages.

title: 制度在禮
summary: 制度在禮，文為在禮；行之，其在人乎？

title: Regulations for Sacrifice / 制祭祀
summary: The sage-kings' criteria for establishing sacrificial systems based on service to the people.

title: 力無敵於天下
summary: 有力不用，力乃真有力；有名出者，違師教而顯能

title: 力與命之辯
summary: 力自謂能制壽夭貴賤，命則謂莫之制而自運。

title: 功遂身退 / Accomplishment Achieved, Withdraw the Self
summary: The Daoist principle that one should retire after achieving success, following natural heavenly order.

title: 加隆倍之
summary: 父母之恩加隆，故服再期而倍之。

title: The Ten Principles of Sacrifice / 十倫
summary: The "Ji Tong" chapter outlines ten ethical principles embodied in sacrificial ritual, ranging from one's relationship with spirits to social hierarchies.

title: 升堂入室
summary: 學道由淺入深，如入門升堂以入於室也。

title: 博學詳說
summary: 博學而詳說者，將以反說約也。

title: The Divination Question: Righteousness or Intention? / 卜筮之問
summary: The formal ritual question "Is it righteous? Is it from intention?" used in divination contexts.

title: 厚作斂於百姓
summary: 橫徵暴斂，乃民苦之根。

title: 厚德薄命
summary: 德厚於人而行不加焉，命薄於時而福不逮焉。

title: 厚葬久喪
summary: 聖王制禮，厚葬久喪非以為名，乃稱情而立文。

title: 友其德 / Friendship Based on Virtue
summary: 孟子提出交友之道在於「友其德」，強調友誼當以德行相交，不挾長、不挾貴、不挾兄弟，超越地位與權勢。

title: 反巡故鄉
summary: 鳥獸失群，猶過故鄉而翔回鳴號，況人於父母之親。

title: Reversal as the Movement of the Dao / 反者道之動
summary: The Daoist principle that reversal (反) is the fundamental movement of the Dao, whereby things return to their source.

title: Prohibition of Same-Surname Marriage / 取妻不取同姓
summary: The Confucian principle prohibiting marriage between individuals of the same surname to maintain distinction and prevent incest.

title: 取象天地
summary: 禮制上象天，下法地，中則人，以成群居之和。

title: 口惠而實不至 / Promises Without Fulfillment / 口惠みして實際に至らざること
summary: The Confucian warning that verbal kindness without material substance invites resentment, and that fulfilling promises宁可招怨 is preferable to false诺言.

title: 古莽之國
summary: 西極之南有國，五旬一覺，以夢為實，以覺為妄，與中土相反也。

title: 可殺而不可辱
summary: 儒者以人格尊嚴為重，視死亡猶可受，而屈辱則不可受。

title: 司射 / Director of Archery (Shooting Officer)
summary: The ritual official who oversees the Pitch-Pot game, responsible for measuring the vessel placement, directing throws, counting scores, and managing the flow of the ceremony.

title: 合巹而酳 / The Shared Cup Ceremony / 婚禮の儀礼
summary: 昏禮中夫婦共用一瓠瓜剖分之酒杯飲酒的儀式，象徵合為一體。

title: 合志同方營道同術
summary: 儒者交友，以志同道合為基礎，道不同則相與退。

title: 同道
summary: 賢人同道，師也父兄、臣也微者，皆可以易地皆然。

title: 名可強立 / Fame Can Be Forcibly Established / 名は強いて立つ可し
summary: Wenzi's assertion that fame and achievement can be actively pursued and established through earnest effort, exemplified by Nanrong Chou.

title: 君以民為體 / The Ruler as Body, the People as Heart
summary: The ruler and people are interdependent like body and heart; damage to one affects the other, requiring mutual care and preservation.

title: 君子不由
summary: 伯夷隘，柳下惠不恭，隘與不恭，君子不由。言中行之道，介於二者之間者為貴。

title: 君子五教 / Five Types of Teaching by the Superior Person / 君子五教
summary: Mencius's classification of five methods by which the junzi imparts teaching,

title: 君子所為
summary: 君子之行，非眾人所能識；務在其志，不在其跡。

title: The Gentleman Compares Virtue to Jade / 君子比德於玉
summary: Confucius's famous metaphor comparing the gentleman's virtues to the qualities of jade, enumerating eleven attributes of jade as models for moral cultivation.

title: 君子無物而不在禮
summary: 君子動靜語默，皆不離乎禮，無物不在其中。

title: 周公致政 / The Duke of Zhou's Return of Authority
summary: 記周公攝政七年還政於成王之事，以周公有勳勞於天下故也。

title: 周公踐位 / The Duke of Zhou Assumed the Ruler's Position
summary: The Duke of Zhou's assumption of the Son of Heaven's position during the minority of King Cheng and his subsequent contributions to ritual establishment.

title: 和者陰陽調 / Harmony: Yin and Yang in Balance
summary: The Daoist principle that harmony (和) is the greatest force between heaven and earth, achieved through the balance of yin and yang.

title: 哀樂相生
summary: 哀與樂相互感發，詩禮樂之至在乎情之流通。

title: 哀痛未盡思慕未忘
summary: 二十五月喪畢，哀痛思慕猶存，乃人情之常。

title: 哭者為位
summary: 凡為位哭者，視親疏遠近而別哭之禮。

title: 哭踊有節 / Regulation of Mourning Crying and Foot-Stamping / 哭踊有節
summary: The principle that mourning rituals require measured crying and foot-stamping with proper节制.

title: 哭辟市朝
summary: 奔喪過國，哭於野以避市朝。

title: The Shang Sacrificial Officer / 商祝
summary: The ritual specialist who performs the principal mourning rites for the deceased, distinct from other ceremonial officers.

title: 問卜筮 / On Inquiring About Divination
summary: Ritual guidelines for asking about divination, distinguishing between righteousness and personal will.

title: 善人
summary: 善人不行聖跡，不能入室；聖人則不然。

title: 善問者如攻堅木
summary: 善問之方，先易後難，及其久則自然通解。

title: 善學者師逸功倍
summary: 善學者，師不勤而功倍，且歸功於師。

title: 善待問者如撞鐘
summary: 善答問者，如鐘之待叩，叩小則小鳴，叩大則大鳴。

title: 善歌使人繼其聲
summary: 善教者使人樂於傳承其志，如善歌者使人繼其聲。

title: 嚴師難得
summary: 天下之尊師，難得而可貴。

title: 四代器服 / Ritual Vessels and Garments Across the Four Dynasties
summary: 記有虞、夏后氏、殷、周四代所用禮器、祭服之異同，以見聖人因時損益之意。

title: The Theory of the Four Origins / 四始之說
summary: 列子's cosmological doctrine describing the four stages of creation from non-breath (太易) through primordial substance (太素), culminating in the separation of heaven and earth.

title: The Four Seasonal Sacrifices / 四時之祭
summary: The four seasonal sacrificial rites — Yue, Di, Shang, and Zheng — embody the balance of yin and yang throughout the year.

title: 四端
summary: 惻隱、羞惡、辭讓、是非之心，乃仁義禮智之端，猶人之有四肢，擴充則可保四海。

title: Four Principles of Mourning / 喪服四製
summary: The four governing principles of mourning rituals: benevolence, righteousness, propriety, and adaptability.

title: 四靈 / The Four Spiritual Creatures / 四霊
summary: The four spiritual animals (unicorn, phoenix, turtle, dragon) that serve as tokens of good governance and cosmic harmony in Confucian tradition.

title: 回何敢死
summary: 夫子以為顏淵死，顏淵則言子在故不敢死。

title: 圃澤東里
summary: 圃澤多賢，東里多才

title: 國無三年之食者國非其國
summary: 備荒儲粟，國家存亡之要務。

title: 地道迎穴
summary: 敵為穴以入，我亟遣穴師迎而穴之，內弩以待。

title: Fang Ji / 坊記
summary: A chapter from the Book of Rites (Liji) discussing the preventive function of ritual in governing the people.

title: 城上之備
summary: 城上守具之名：渠譫、藉車、行棧、行樓、頡皋、連梃、長斧、長椎、長茲、距、飛衝、縣𠊱。

title: 城上備渠譫
summary: 城上之渠、譫，乃防敵攻城之要具。

title: 城上持出必操填章
summary: 城中之人持物出城，必持符印為驗，否則禁止。

title: 城上火備
summary: 城上置火之具，蓄水、薪、突火，以防火攻並拒敵人。

summary: The Confucian code of conduct for ministers serving their lords, emphasizing remonstrance without slander and loyalty.

title: 為天下容 / Containing the World: The Virtues of the Ruler
summary: A famous passage describing the nine qualities necessary for a ruler to "contain" or properly govern the world.

title: Ritual as Carving Human Nature / 為禮者雕琢人性
summary: Wenzi's critique of ritual as an artificial constraint on natural human nature that prevents fulfillment.

title: 為至痛極
summary: 創深痛甚者日彌久，三年之制，乃為至痛而設。

title: 無服為位
summary: 無喪服之親而為位哭者，唯嫂叔及降服之婦。

title: 無樂無知
summary: 絕去喜怒嗜欲，復歸本性之真樂真知

title: 燕禮 / The Banquet Ritual (燕禮)
summary: 諸侯朝聘之後與群臣共食之禮，以明君臣之義、辨貴賤之分。

title: 燕義 / The Meaning of the Banquet Ritual / 燕義
summary: A chapter of the Book of Rites explaining the ritual principles and political significance of the state banquet.

title: 父在父主父沒兄弟主
summary: 喪主之禮，父在則父主，父沒則兄弟同居各主其喪。

title: 父母三年
summary: 子生三年免於父母懷，故為父母服三年之喪。

title: 牛山之木 / The Trees of Niu Mountain
summary: Mencius's famous analogy comparing the human heart to the trees on Niu Mountain, which once were beautiful but were stripped bare by axes and grazing.

title: 物不至者則不反
summary: 物未極則不知返，患未至則不知戒

title: 狸首 / Li Shou (Fox-Head Melody)
summary: The ceremonial music piece played during the Pitch-Pot ritual, referenced in the Book of Rites as the accompaniment for archery-related ceremonies.

title: 獨善其身 / Self-Cultivation in Obscurity / 独善其身
summary: The Confucian ideal of maintaining personal virtue when unable to serve publicly, contrasted with the ideal of benefiting all when one's talents are realized.

title: The Way of Mystery / 玄道
summary: The eternal mystery that is the origin of nature and the foundation of all existence, accessible only to those who attain inner understanding.

title: Leading Beasts to Devour People / 率獸食人
summary: 孟子斥梁惠王之政，謂庖廚肥美而民有饑色，猶率獸以食人，非民之父母所為。

title: Jade Ornaments of the Son of Heaven / 天子玉藻
summary: The jade ornaments worn by the Son of Heaven, symbolizing virtue and the cosmic order, with twelve tasseled strands representing the twelve months.

title: A King's Words Begin Like Silk Thread, End Like a Ribbon / 王言如絲，其出如綸
summary: A Confucian maxim warning that the ruler's words, though small in origin, grow immensely in influence as they spread, urging rulers to exercise utmost caution in speech.

title: The Theory of Self-Generation and Self-Transformation / 生化之說
summary: 列子's doctrine that all things generate and transform themselves without external intervention, rooted in the principle that the ungenerated generates and the untransformed transforms.

title: 生相憐，死相捐 / Compassionate in Life, Releasing in Death
summary: A Liezi Yang Zhu maxim on proper conduct toward the living (providing care and comfort) versus the dead (free release without display).

title: 由生而生
summary: 生死皆有其道，常與不幸之別也

title: 男女有別 / Gender Distinction as the Basis of Social Order
summary: The distinction between male and female is the foundation from which conjugal duty, filial affection, and proper governance all derive.

title: The Hunchback Catching Cicadas / 痀僂承蜩
summary: 痀僂者以五月之法累丸二而不墜，專志凝神，終以捕蟬如拾取。孔子稱其「用志不分，乃疑於神」。

title: 發梁擒敵
summary: 城外塹中施發梁機，敵渡則引機發梁以擒之。

title: 發而不中反求諸己 / Archery Failure Calls for Self-Examination / 射而不中、反って己を求む
summary: 射而不中，不怨勝己者，當反求諸己，此射道之要義，亦修身之通理。

title: 白圭之誡
summary: 南容誦白圭而謹言，夫子以其慎行妻之。

title: The True Person / 真人
summary: The Daoist ideal of the "true person" (真人) who has achieved unity with the Dao through emptiness, tranquility, and pure simplicity.

title: 知幻化之不異生死
summary: 幻化與生死，本無差異。悟此者，可以學幻矣。

title: 知言
summary: 能辨詖、淫、邪、遁之辭，知其所蔽、陷、離、窮，斯可以知聖人矣。

title: The She and Ji Altars / 社稷
summary: The altars to the soil deity and grain spirit representing the foundation of the state.

title: 神遊形奚動哉
summary: 精神可遊於異境，形骸不隨之而往。夢中為君，覺亦夢也。

title: Distinction Between Spirits and Ghosts / 神鬼之辨
summary: The classical Chinese philosophical distinction between "神" (spirits/divinities) and "鬼" (ghosts), based on their beneficial or non-beneficial nature to humanity.

title: 祭不欲數疏 / Moderation in Sacrifice: Neither Too Frequent Nor Too Rare
summary: 祭有常節，數則煩，疏則怠，君子合諸天道，春禘秋嘗。

title: The Ten Categories of Sacrifice / 祭有十倫
summary: The ten principles or meanings embodied in proper sacrificial ritual, including relationships with spirits, rulers, family, and social hierarchy.

title: Seasonal Sacrifices / 祭有四時：礿禘嘗烝
summary: The four seasonal sacrifice ceremonies—Yue, Di, Chang, and Zheng—and their cosmological significance.

title: Laws of Sacrifice / 祭法
summary: The sacrificial laws and principles from the Book of Rites covering ancestral worship, spirit veneration, and the criteria for who deserves sacrifice.

title: Sacrificing to the Hundred Spirits / 祭百神
summary: The doctrine that rulers of all-under-heaven should offer sacrifices to the hundred spirits according to their domain.

title: Sacrifice as the Root of Filial Piety / 祭者孝之本
summary: The "Record of Rites" declares that sacrifice is the foundation of filial piety, linking ritual practice to the cultivation of virtue.

title: Sacrifice Originates from the Heart / 祭者非物自外至者，自中出於心也
summary: The doctrine that ritual sacrifice springs from inner moral feeling rather than external obligation.

title: Sacrifice Arises from the Heart / 祭者非自外至
summary: The philosophical principle that sacrifice originates internally from genuine heartfelt reverence rather than from external obligations.

title: 禮之五用 / The Five Functions of Ritual: Clarifying Social Relations
summary: The five ritual occasions—court audiences, diplomatic visits, mourning, village assemblies, and marriage—clarify the essential relationships of society.

title: 禮之所興
summary: 禮之所興，眾之所治；禮之所廢，眾之所亂。

title: The Subtle Transforming Power of Ritual / 禮之教化也微
summary: The Confucian doctrine that proper ritual education transforms people imperceptibly, leading them toward goodness without their conscious awareness.

title: Using Ritual to Dam Up Virtue / 禮以坊德
summary: A principle from the Book of Rites advocating ritual propriety as a preventive mechanism against moral decline.

title: 禮器與盛德 / Ritual Vessels and Abundant Virtue
summary: The concept that proper ritual vessels express and embody moral virtue, making completeness possible.

title: 禮坊止水 / Ritual as a Dam: Preventing Social Disorder Before It Arises
summary: Confucius compares ritual to a dam that prevents the flood of chaos, warning against abandoning traditional rites.

title: Reciprocity in Ritual / 禮尚往來
summary: The Confucian principle that courtesy should be reciprocated—giving without receiving, or receiving without giving, violates ritual propriety.

title: 禮所以制中
summary: 禮者，所以節制人情，使其無過不及也。

title: 禮樂不可斯須去身 / Ritual and Music Cannot Be Absent Even for a Moment / 禮楽は斯くの間も身を離るべからず
summary: The Confucian principle that ritual propriety and music must be constantly present in one's person as essential means of moral cultivation.

title: Ritual Prevents Chaos at Its Source / 禮禁亂之所由生
summary: The doctrine that ritual (li) functions to prevent social disorder by addressing its origins, comparing it to a dam against flooding.

title: 禮者治之治
summary: 禮者，即事之治也。治國而無禮，則無以相也。

title: 禮者理也
summary: 禮者，理也；樂者，節也。無理不動，無節不作。

title: 禮者領惡全好
summary: 禮者，領惡而全好，所以仁鬼神、仁昭穆、仁死喪、仁鄉黨、仁賓客。

title: The Monthly Ordinances of the Book of Rites / 禮記月令
summary: A classical Chinese text describing the seasonal governmental duties and rituals for each month of the year.

title: 稱情而立文
summary: 禮文當依人情而立，以飾等威別親疏，不可增減。

title: 立中制節
summary: 先王立適中之道，以節人情，使文理可成。

title: Ceremonial Tablet / 朝笏之制
summary: The ceremonial tablet (笏) held by officials in court, with specifications varying by rank from jade for the Son of Heaven to bamboo for scholars.

title: Ritual Ploughing / 籍田禮
summary: The ancient Chinese ceremony in which the Son of Heaven personally ploughed a sacred field to symbolize imperial concern for agriculture.

title: 精誠 / Sincerity and Spiritual Power / 精誠
summary: The doctrine that inner sincerity (精誠) generates external transformative power, manifesting cosmic responses to moral governance.

title: 絜矩之道
summary: 治天下者當以己之心度人之心，上下左右無所乖戾。

title: 緇衣 / The Black Robe
summary: 《禮記》篇名，以「好賢如緇衣」為發端，論述君臣、君子之交及治國之道。

title: Climbing a Tree to Catch Fish / 緣木求魚
summary: 孟子以緣木求魚喻齊宣王欲闢土地朝秦楚之妄，謂以若所為求若所欲必有災。

title: 縣火
summary: 懸火以禦敵入之術。

title: 義與信和與仁 / Righteousness, Trust, Harmony, and Benevolence: The Four Virtues of Governance
summary: The four political virtues—harmony, benevolence, trust, and righteousness—constitute the essential instruments of hegemon-kings.

title: 聖之時者 / The Sage Who Moves with the Times
summary: 孔子被孟子稱為「聖之時者」，與伯夷（聖之清者）、伊尹（聖之任者）、柳下惠（聖之和者）並稱，喻其能因時制宜，進退自如。

title: 聖人
summary: 自生民以來，未有孔子。伯夷、伊尹、孔子皆古聖人，而孔子集其大成。

title: 聖王不為樂
summary: 墨子答程繁之問，謂古之聖王有其樂而簡，故不以此治天下；樂繁則治寡，非所以為治也。

title: 聘問 / Inter-State Diplomatic Missions
summary: The ancient Chinese system of diplomatic visits between the Son of Heaven and feudal lords.

title: Meaning of Diplomatic Missions / 聘義
summary: A chapter of the Book of Rites explaining the philosophical foundations of inter-state diplomatic missions and the virtue of respect-yielding.

title: 聞善相告見善相示
summary: 儒者聞善必相告，見善必相示，患難相死，久相待也。

title: 聞喪不得奔
summary: 不得奔喪而為位哭，與奔喪者禮同。

title: 聞斯行之
summary: 聞義而行，當視人之稟性進退，不可一概而論。

title: 聞遠兄弟之喪
summary: 遠方兄弟之喪，於除服後乃聞，當免袒成踴。

title: 聲聞過情
summary: 名過乎實，君子恥之。

title: The Way of Sound and Music Reflects Governance / 聲音之道與政通
summary: The classical doctrine that musical expression is inseparable from political order and moral condition.

title: 聽天下之內治 / Governing the Internal Affairs / 天下の内部を治める
summary: 后率六宮以治天下之內治，乃昏禮申著代之意所延伸之王化原理。

title: 聽天下之外治 / Governing the External Affairs / 天下の外部を治める
summary: 天子立六官以聽天下之外治，與后治內治相須而成治道。

title: 聽語
summary: 記問之學不足為師，必也聽語，俟其不能問而後告之。

title: 肆之而已，勿壅勿閼 / Abandon All Restraint, Block Nothing
summary: Guan Yiwu's doctrine of life-nourishment taught to Yan Ying, prescribing complete release of sensory and desire-based restraints.

title: 能仁而不能反
summary: 各有所長亦各有所短，兼四子之有以易吾，吾弗許

title: Humbling Oneself and Honoring Others / 自卑而尊人
summary: The principle that ritual requires lowering oneself while honoring others.

title: 自求多福
summary: 禍福無不自己求之者，天作孽猶可違，自作孽不可活。

title: 自生自死
summary: 生死厚薄，非由外鑠，皆自為之。

title: The Supreme Person / 至人
summary: The transcendent person who has realized the Way, dwells beyond worldly honor and shame, and moves freely between the mundane and the divine.

title: 至死不窮
summary: 血氣之屬莫知於人，故人於其親，哀慕至死而不已。

title: 至親以期斷
summary: 至親之喪，以一期為斷，示天地四時已更。

title: Utmost Sincerity and the Fulfillment of Nature / 至誠盡性
summary: A Confucian doctrine that attaining utmost sincerity enables one to fulfill one's nature, others' natures, and all things' natures, thereby participating in the transforming work of heaven and earth.

title: Reverence Persists and Manifests / 致愛則存，致愨則著
summary: Deep love preserves the beloved in memory; sincere reverence makes the deceased manifest—both ensure that neither is forgotten.

title: 致樂以治心 / Using Music to Cultivate the Heart / 楽以心を治める
summary: The Confucian doctrine that thorough application of music serves as a primary means of cultivating and governing the human heart-mind.

title: 致知在格物
summary: 天下之達喪，禮之極也，而源於人心自然之情。

title: 與人為善
summary: 大舜善與人同，樂取於人以為善，君子莫大乎與人為善。

title: 與民同樂
summary: Mencius argued that a true king shares joy and sorrow with his people; ruling together brings happiness, while ruling apart brings suffering.

title: 舍生取義 / Choosing Righteousness over Life
summary: A central Mencian doctrine that when life and righteousness cannot both be preserved, one must choose righteousness.

title: 良冶學為裘
summary: 良匠之子必學世業以通其道，教人亦當因其所能而啟之。

title: Tyranny Is Fiercer Than Tigers / 苛政猛於虎
summary: A parable about a woman who refuses to leave an area where tigers have killed multiple family members, because even worse than tigers is harsh government.

title: 苟有車必見其軾 / Words and Actions Are Inseparable
summary: The principle that speech and action are inherently linked, like a cart and its crossbar, cannot be separated.

title: 苦逸之復數之常
summary: 苦者夢逸、逸者夢苦，迭為消長，理之常也。

title: Four Grades of Talent / 英俊豪傑
summary: A Daoist classification of talented individuals into four grades based on their virtues and capabilities.

title: 莊敬日強 / Dignified Respect Strengthens Daily / 莊敬は日を強くす
summary: The principle that dignified respect and solemnity lead to daily moral strengthening, while complacency leads to decline.

title: The Yellow Emperor's Dream of Huaxu / 華胥之夢
summary: 黃帝齋心三月，夢遊華胥氏之國，乃悟至道不可以情求，遂致天下大治。

title: 萬物皆備於我 / All Things Are Complete Within Me / 萬物皆備於我
summary: A core Mencian teaching that all virtues and moral capacities are inherently present within every person, requiring only reflective inquiry to realize them.

title: All Things Emerge from the Mechanism / 萬物皆出於機
summary: The doctrine that all things in the universe emerge from and return to a primordial mechanism or pivot, illustrated through an elaborate chain of transformations from plants to animals to humans.

title: 薪柴杜外
summary: 城外薪木柴搏，廣厚足以任城，以堵禦敵人之攻城器械。

title: 藏焉修焉息焉游焉
summary: 君子之於學，藏之於心，修之於行，息之於暇，游之於時。

title: Emptiness and Tranquility / 虛無恬淡
summary: The Daoist state of inner emptiness and tranquility as the foundation for wisdom and proper action.

title: 蛾傅
summary: 蛾傅，敵人蟻聚攻城之術，廣五百步、上術三千人。

title: 行一不義殺一不辜
summary: 得百里之地而君之，皆能朝諸侯有天下；然行一不義、殺一不辜而得天下，皆不為也。

title: 行城法
summary: 為行城以禦攻之術。

title: 術不可不慎
summary: 矢人函人之殊，在於術之慎不慎。里仁為美，擇不處仁，不得為智。

title: 襚者 / The Garment-Presenter in Funeral Rites / 襚者（さいしゃ）
summary: The ritual specialist who presents burial garments to the deceased, a key figure in ancient Chinese funeral ceremonies recorded in the Book of Rites.

title: 西方有聖
summary: 孔子稱道西方之聖，不治而不亂

title: 規矩繩權衡 / Compass, Square, Cord, Weight, and Balance
summary: 深衣之製所象徵之五器，以應規、矩、繩、權、衡，取其無私、直、平之義。

title: 視學 / Royal Inspection of Education
summary: 天子視學，大昕鼓徵，祭先師先聖，遂設三老五更之席位。

title: Graduated Kinship Mourning / 親親以三為五，以五為九
summary: The principle of graduated mourning obligations based on kinship distance, extending from immediate family to the ninth degree.

slug: 言從而行之行從而言之
title: When Speech Follows Action, Words Cannot Be Concealed; When Action Follows Speech, Deeds Cannot Be Hidden / 言從而行之，則言不可飾也；行從而言之，則行不可飾也
summary: A Confucian principle that one's words reveal one's actions, and one's actions reveal one's words, demanding congruence between speech and conduct for moral authority.

title: 言而履之禮
summary: 言而履之謂之禮，行而樂之謂之樂。

title: The Beauty of Ceremonial Expressions / 言語之美
summary: The aesthetic standards for different ritual contexts described in the "Minor Rules of Deportment."

title: 誠
summary: 誠者，天之道；誠之者，人之道。至誠能盡其性，贊天地之化育，是為聖人之極功。

sources.question: 何謂誠？儒家以誠為何物？
sources.title: 何謂誠？儒家以誠為何物？

title: 誠意
summary: 意念發動之時，直臻真實，不容自欺

title: On Speaking to Great Men / 說大人則藐之
summary: Mencius advises speaking fearlessly to great ministers by despising their external grandeur and focusing on moral principles, establishing the dignity of the scholar against worldly power.

title: 論篤色莊
summary: 論議篤實者未必皆君子，色莊者亦未可遽信。

title: 貉道
summary: 欲輕堯舜之賦者，大貉小貉也；欲重之者，大桀小桀也。

title: 負繩及踝 / Back Cord Reaching the Ankle
summary: 深衣背縫下垂至踝，取象繩墨之直，以象正道直行無邪。

title: 財不足則反之時，食不足則反之用
summary: 理財之道，在乎審時節用。

title: 賞行罰
summary: 賞罰以靜爲故從之以急之法。

title: 赗 / Funeral Carriage Gifts / 賵（ほう）
summary: The ritual of presenting carriages and horses as condolence gifts in ancient Chinese funerals, documented in the Book of Rites.

title: 赤子之心
summary: 大人之心，純一如赤子，不失其本真。

title: 身可危而志不可奪
summary: 儒者雖陷於危難，身命或有不保，而心志堅定不可動搖。

title: Imperial Ploughing Ceremony / 躬耕帝藉
summary: The ritual in which the emperor personally ploughed the sacred fields to demonstrate reverence for agriculture and to urge the people to cultivate the land.

title: The Beauty of Speech, Court, Sacrifice, and Horses / 穆穆皇皇之美
summary: The fourfold beauty described in the Book of Rites encompassing elegant speech, orderly court, solemn sacrifice, and majestic horses.

title: Valuing Ritual Over Wealth / 輕財重禮
summary: The Confucian principle that ritual propriety should be valued above material wealth, with implications for both personal conduct and interstate relations.

title: 辨貴賤長幼
summary: 昔聖帝明王辨貴賤長幼遠近男女內外，皆由此途出。

title: The Spring Welcoming Ceremony / 迎春之禮
summary: A seasonal ritual in which the emperor welcomed spring at the eastern suburb, embodying the unity of heaven and human governance.

title: Seasonal Welcoming Rituals / 迎氣
summary: The ancient Chinese court ritual of welcoming the seasonal qi at the four directional suburbs.

title: 送死有已復生有節
summary: 送死有節，復生有期，喪期已盡，當復其常。

title: 送死當大事
summary: 養生之禮易盡，送死之誠難盡，故送死可以當大事。

title: 造父學御 / 造父が御を嗜む
summary: A parable about mastering chariot driving through concentration, proper posture, and harmony between driver and horse.

title: Diplomatic Meeting Categories / 遇會聘誓盟——諸侯外交會見之制
summary: The five categories of inter-state diplomatic engagements in Zhou ritual protocol: ad hoc meetings, scheduled assemblies, envoys, oaths, and covenants.

title: 過則改之
summary: 君子有過，如日月之食，人皆見之；及其改也，人皆仰之。

title: 過猶不及
summary: 過與不及，其失相同；中道者，善之美也。

title: 道而弗牽
summary: 教人當引導之而不強拽之，使學者樂於趨道。

title: Hemp Mourning Garments for Officials / 錫衰
summary: The hemp mourning attire prescribed for rulers and ministers during official duties and mourning periods.

title: Mourning Attire for Officials / 錫衰以居
summary: Regulations governing hair-cloth mourning garments for ministers and officials during official duties.

title: 長善救失
summary: 教育之本，在於發揚人之善端，救正人之過失。

title: 開而弗達
summary: 啟發之而不遽告之，使學者深思而自得。

title: 閔子侍側
summary: 閔子、子路、冉有、子貢，各有氣象，夫子樂之。

title: 附庸 / Vassal States and Subordinate Territories
summary: The feudal hierarchy of minor states attached to greater lords in ancient China.

title: 陳仲子 / Chen Zhongzi
summary: 孟子批判陳仲子之「廉」，指出其操守超越常人但不可推廣，如同蚯蚓方能完全踐行其道。

title: 陽里華子病忘
summary: 華子中年病忘，忘則無憂；及其痊愈，反以記憶為苦。忘之與記，孰得失耶？

title: 負子汲井之喻
summary: 見死不救，悖於人情。

title: 雲梯之守
summary: 禦雲梯攻城之總術。

title: Instruments of Hegemon-Kings / 霸王之器
summary: The doctrine that righteousness, trust, harmony, and benevolence are the essential "vessels" for hegemons and true kings to govern.

title: The Way of Hegemon-Kings / 霸王之道
summary: 文子論霸道之要義，以謀略輔義，非圖自存，乃救亡平亂、除暴安民。

title: 靜以脩身 / Self-Cultivation Through Stillness
summary: A Daoist principle advocating stillness (靜) as the foundation for personal cultivation and governmental harmony.

title: 非助我者
summary: 顏淵於夫子之言無所不悅，非助於教者也。

title: 非獨賢者有是心 / Not Only the Worthy Possess This Heart
summary: Mencius's assertion that the moral capacity for righteousness is universal to all humans, not a privilege of the sage.

title: 顏淵之葬
summary: 顏淵死，門人厚葬之，夫子以為非己所能止。

title: 顏淵好學短命
summary: 顏淵好學而不幸短命，夫子深惜之。

title: 食者人之本 / Food: The Root of the People
summary: The principle that food is the foundation of the people, and agriculture the basis of governance, advocating sustainable resource management.

title: Rice Dumplings and Wild Herbs / 舜之飯糗茹草
summary: Mencius illustrates contentment and virtue through the story of Shun eating coarse food and wearing grass clothes before becoming emperor.

title: Nourishing the Heart Through Few Desires / 養心莫善於寡欲
summary: Mencius teaches that cultivating the mind is best achieved by reducing desires, using a vivid quantitative comparison to show the inverse relationship between desire and moral preservation.

title: 養老之禮 / Rites for the Elderly / 养老の礼
summary: The comprehensive system of honoring, supporting, and caring for the elderly at various life stages, as codified in classical Confucian texts.

title: The Post-Sacrifice Feast (Jun) / 餕
summary: The "Jun" feast, eaten after the sacrificial ceremony, represents the final and democratic phase of the ritual, distributing blessings to all participants regardless of rank.

title: 魯兼用四代 / Lu's Comprehensive Adoption of the Four Dynasties
summary: The state of Lu's unique synthesis of ritual vessels, music, officials, and institutions from the Four Dynasties—、有虞氏、夏、殷、周.

title: 魯用天子禮樂 / Lu State's Use of Son of Heaven's Rituals
summary: 記魯國受命用天子禮樂祀周公，乃殊榮也，以見禮制之隆。

title: 鳴鼓而攻
summary: 冉有為季氏聚斂，夫子怒而絕之。

title: Hemp with Root: Transformation of Mourning Attire / 麻之有本與三年之葛
summary: The doctrine that hemp cloth with its root intact transforms three-year mourning garments, marking transitions between mourning periods.

title: Inscriptions on Ritual Vessels / 鼎銘
summary: The Confucian practice of inscribing bronze vessels with records of ancestors' virtue and achievements, serving as a means of moral education and familial remembrance.

title: 齊家
summary: 以德化一家，使父子兄弟各盡其道

title: 龍斷
summary: 商人專擅市利，征商之法自此始。
